channel.title: Live Miracles blog
channel.description: Notes from running live events and building the tools behind them.

item.title: Our vMix presets kept breaking on renamed files, so we stopped building them by hand
item.description: Hand-built vMix presets break when a file is renamed and drift when someone changes an audio setting. Folder Player builds the preset from a numbered folder and a base preset instead, so every session starts clean.

item.title: A full web controller for vMix: control everything from your browser
item.description: vMix's built-in Web Controller is minimal. vMix Master is a free, extensive web controller laid out like vMix itself, so you can run or support a vMix from any browser, and switch several vMix systems together when you need to.

item.title: Live Q&A in many languages: one list instead of a chat per language
item.description: Running a live Q&A when every language has its own Zoom or YouTube chat? Multi Lang QA is a free Google Apps Script app that puts all the questions, translated, into one list for the teacher.

item.title: One faulty audio embedder disrupted a mega event
item.description: Two fiber paths carried the same bad audio, while our monitoring missed the cancellation between left and right channels.

item.title: SRS, MediaMTX and Restreamer reject bonded SRT. Here is a relay that fixes it
item.description: SRS, MediaMTX and Restreamer reject a bonded SRT group. So we added a small de-bonding relay Goryu in front and, and it worked.

item.title: 50 inputs and 500 outputs in one dashboard
item.description: A look at Bunryu's dashboard with 50 live inputs and 500 output destinations, including how problems appear and how many server resources the control plane uses.

item.title: One leaking FFmpeg process took down six live streams
item.description: A memory leak in one FFmpeg process restarted our whole streaming stack. How it happened, and the guard rails that keep a single bad process small.
